# Mission and Repository Facts

Boruch Hashem. Blessed is He.

> The Awtsmoos gives the project no permission to pretend: reality on disk is the vessel, evidence is the light, and Awtsmoos.com must be improved by what is actually observed rather than imagined.

## Mission

Unify the movie-making capabilities under `geelooy` so 2D and 3D authoring share a dependable declarative movie contract while each application keeps its own product personality. Make AI able to author real timed scenes containing characters, cameras, text, shapes, animated paths, particles, infographic/tutorial choreography, 2D and 3D content, audio/captions, transitions, and exportable output. Improve mobile-first authoring. Produce and verify a real 180-second demonstration movie.

## Directly observed facts

- Repository root inspected: `/Users/awtsmoos/work/awtsmoos.com`.
- Target root inspected: `geelooy`.
- App inventory includes `animator`, `mitzvah-studio`, `nesher-studio`, `video-editor`, `slides`, and shared libraries.
- `animator` already contains AI command routing, camera planning, character systems, rendering pipelines, studio authoring, procedural generators, movie export, and verification tools.
- The working tree is heavily dirty before this mission begins.
- Many Animator files are already modified by concurrent work, including AI, rendering, character, camera, export, and mobile authoring files.
- Mitzvah Studio also has existing uncommitted UI changes.
- Unrelated server, tunnel, game, piano, and site files are modified by other work.
- Therefore no reset, cleanup, blind overwrite, or broad formatting pass is permitted.

## Concurrency safety rule

Every source file considered for modification must be re-read immediately before a whole-file rewrite. Existing modifications are treated as current project reality. New shared modules are preferred where they can reduce collision risk. If a currently modified app file is necessary, its live contents and direct callers/tests must be inspected first.

## Acceptance evidence required

1. Exact movie-capable surfaces discovered from real imports, exports, docs, and runtime paths.
2. A shared movie contract with distinct application profiles/adapters.
3. AI-facing commands/schema that can create and mutate meaningful movie timelines rather than returning placeholders.
4. 2D and 3D scene capabilities represented consistently.
5. Mobile-first authoring behavior verified at narrow viewport widths.
6. A 180-second demo plan using many scenes, characters, particles, shapes, paths, text, infographic/tutorial beats, and varied camera shots.
7. Export or deterministic render artifact verified as a real movie output using the repository's available encoding path.
8. Static, unit/integration, smoke, and browser checks pass for touched surfaces.
9. All touched source files re-read after writing; imports, tabs, line counts, syntax, and runtime behavior checked.

## Initial remaining work

- Discover the complete movie-capability graph.
- Inspect shared 2D/3D libraries and app-specific engines.
- Compare existing AI protocols and timeline/export models.
- Select the least-collision shared architecture.
- Implement in complete files only.
- Build the 180-second feature-dense movie.
- Test, render, inspect, and close discovered deltas.
